column2: To the teacher one should give double, with the pavilion and the rest as before. Destruction of sin and supreme accomplishment come by the consecration of a grove of trees.
Hear the consecration and the rest as Ishana told it to Skanda: of the Sun, Ishana, Ganesha, Shakti and the rest, and of Hari's retinue.
One should worship the Gana, the teacher, the sandals, Shakti, Ananta and Dharma; the principal bone-circle and the lower and upper coverings.
One should worship the lotus-pericarp seed-syllables and Jvalini with Nanda; Suryesha, Kamarupa, Udaya, Kamavartini,
Satya and Vighnanasha; the seat of scent and clay; "Yam" the drier, "Ram" the burner, "Lam" the flood, "Vam" likewise nectar.
We know the pot-bellied; we meditate on the great-bellied; may the tusked one urge us on that. Ganapati, Ganadhipa, Ganesha, Gananayaka,
Ganakrida, Vakratunda, Ekadamshtra, Mahodara, Gajavaktra, Lambukukshi, Vikata, Vighnanashana. The dark-colored one, Mahendra and the others are remembered as to be worshipped for Ganapati.
Mantra-bathing is thus, of Varuna and Agni too: with the mind, with the root-mantra, preceded by breath-control,
one should do the mental bath, which is prescribed everywhere. In Vaishnava and other rites one should do bathing and the rest with their own mantras.
I shall tell the rule of twilight prayers with various mantras together, O Guha: having looked, one should drink water thrice at the Brahma-tirtha with the Shankara mantras,
with endings of svadha and the principles of the Self and the rest; then one should touch the openings with the heart; having done the dividing, established by breath-control,
the mantra-master should repeat thrice with the mind the Shiva-samhita. Having rinsed and made the placement, in the morning one should recall Brahmi Sandhya,
seated on a swan-lotus seat, red, four-faced, four-armed, with a flowing garland on the right, on the left a staff and water-pot.
At midday one should meditate on Vaishnavi, white, on a Garuda-lotus seat, bearing conch and discus on the left and on the right mace and fearlessness.
One should meditate on Raudri seated on a bull-lotus, three-eyed, adorned with a moon, bearing trident and rosary on the right, on the left fearlessness and spear.
Sandhya is the witness of actions, following the Self's radiance; the fourth twilight of the knowers is contemplated at midnight and the rest.
In heart, bindu and Brahma-aperture, the formless one stands beyond; that which is devoted to the knowledge of Shiva is called the highest Sandhya.
The ancestral tirtha is at the root of the forefinger, Prajapati's at the little finger; the Brahma tirtha at the base of the thumb; the divine at the tips of the hand;
on the palm of the right hand fire's tirtha; Soma's on the left; and of the sages in all the finger-joints.
Then having made the tirtha Shiva-natured with Shiva mantras, one should perform the sprinkling with the Samhita mantras with that water.
Joining water falling in the left hand with the right hand, the sprinkling on the head with mantras in order is declared.
Having brought to the tip of the nose the white water of the nature of knowledge held in the cupped right hand, drawing it to the left one should hold it.
One should hurl that sin, looking like collyrium, with the fist onto a thunderbolt rock after exhaling through Pingala; that is Aghamarshana.
With the Shiva mantra ending in svaha, with kusha, flowers and rice, having given an arghya-handful to Shiva, one should repeat the Gayatri according to capacity.
I shall tell the libation at the divine tirtha with mantras: one should satisfy with "Haum, to Shiva," others with svaha.
Ham, to the heart; Hrim, to the head; Hrum, to the crest; Hraim, to the armor; to the missile — the eight divine groups, and the Adityas of the heart,
Ham to the Vasus, then Rudras, Vishvedevas and Maruts, Bhrigus, Ham to the Angirases; then the sages with the sacred thread about the neck.
To Atri, then to Vasishtha, homage, then to Pulastya, to Kratu, to Bharadvaja, homage to Vishvamitra;
to Prachetas, to men; to Sanaka, vashat; "Ham to Sananda, vashat," to Sanatana, vashat;
to Sanatkumara, vashat; to Kapila, vashat; to Panchashikha, to Dyubhu, with joined palm-base;
to all beings, vaushat; the beings, gods and fathers; with the thread on the right shoulder, with sesame at the root and tip of kusha;
to Kavyavala-Anala, to Soma, to Yama, to Aryaman, to Agnisoma, to the Barhishads, with svadha;
to Ajyapa, to Soma, and especially the fathers like the gods. "Om Ham, to Ishana": svadha to the father, to the grandfather;
to the peaceful great-grandfather, and likewise the dead fathers; to the fathers, to the grandfathers, svadha, then to the great-grandfather;
to the elder great-grandfathers and to the mothers svadha; "Ham, to the maternal grandfathers; Ham, to the maternal great-grandfathers";

to the elder maternal great-grandfathers, likewise to all fathers; svadha to all; to kin and to all teachers; to the quarters, guardians of the quarters, the perfected, the mothers, seizers and demons.
Having shown the lotus mudra and bilva mudra, the fire-sacrifice is said by the heart: "Om Am, to the heart, homage; to the Sun, to the head" likewise;
Bhur Bhuvah Svah, to the lord of gods, one should worship to the crest in the southwest; "Hum, to the armor" in the northwest; "Ham, to the eye" in the middle;
Vah, to the missile in the east and so on; then one should show the mudras. The cow-mudra for the heart and the rest, the cow-horn for the eyes,
the frightening one for the missile; and salutation to the planets. "Som" Soma; "Bum" Budha; "Brim" Jiva; "Bham" Bhargava one should worship;
on the petals in the east and the fire direction and others: "Am" Bhauma; "Sham" Shanaishchara; "Ram" Rahu; "Kem" Ketu, with scent and the rest and with space and torch.
Having repeated the root-mantra and given the arghya-vessel water, a praise to the Sun; having bowed, to the Sun facing away one should say "Forgive."
Having struck with the atom of the arrow ending in "phat," withdrawing the atom, in the lotus of the heart, with the Shiva-Surya withdrawer, the purification,
one should unite the radiance to Chanda; one should offer the Sun's leftovers. Having worshipped in Ishana, by repetition, meditation and oblation everything belongs to the Sun.
In the purification of the Self, the materials, the mantra and the linga, one should worship all gods: in the northwest Ganapati; "Ham" to the teachers in Shiva.
One should worship the support-power like a sprout, stationed on the tortoise stone; Shiva's endless seat mounted on the Brahma stone.
Of variegated hair, each looking at the other's back, in the form of Krita, Treta and the rest, Shiva's seat and sandals.
Dharma, knowledge, dispassion and lordship, facing the fire direction, one should worship in order, colored like elbow, saffron, gold and collyrium.
The lotus in the middle of the pericarp, nine in the middle in the east and others; the powers holding fly-whisks with boon-giving and fearless hands:
Vama, Jyeshtha, Raudri, Kali, Kalavikarini, Balavikarini, Balapramathini are to be worshipped in order.
Ham — Sarvabhutadamani at the tip of the filament, Manonmani; the seat pervading the principles from earth up to pure knowledge.
One should place the god on the lion-throne: white, five-faced, pervading, ten-armed, bearing a crescent moon in his right hands:
spear, trident, skull-staff, boon-giving; in his left hands a drum, citron, blue lotus, thread and lotus;
the Shaiva form endowed with thirty-two marks in the middle: "Ham Ham Ham, to Shiva's form," remembering Shiva the self-luminous,
having led the mantra by abandoning the cause beginning with Brahma to Shiva's abode; then, standing in the middle of the forehead, with the radiance of the lord of the shining stars,
filled with the six limbs, Shiva of bindu form, the supreme; having meditated him in the flower-handful, one should place him in the Lakshmi form.
Om Ham Haum, homage to Shiva with the invoking mantra from the heart; having invoked and established, with the establishing, having made Shiva present near,
one should restrain with the harsh Kalakanti ending in "phat"; having driven off obstacles, then the linga mudra and salutation,
one should cover with the heart; afterward the invocation is face-to-face; the placing is establishment; presence is "I am yours, O lord."
Up to the ritual section, presence, and beyond: the manifestation of the devotee's own is the covering.
Having made the fulfillment with the six mantras and then oneness, one should render the limbs with the limbed one nectarized.
The heart of Shambhu's power of consciousness; Shiva's eightfold lordship; control of the crest and the unbreakable radiance; the lordly armor;
the irresistible majesty and the missile that removes obstacles. "Namah, svadha, svaha, vaushat" in order,
having uttered preceded by the heart-mantra one should offer foot-water and the rest: foot-water on the two lotus feet; rinsing-water on the mouths;
arghya on the head of the god, with durva, flowers and rice. Thus having prepared the Supreme Lord by ten rites,
one should worship with the five-fold service by rule, with flowers and the rest; having sprinkled, rubbed, and cleansed with mustard, salt and the like,
one should bathe him slowly with drops of arghya-water and flowers with pots; with milk, curds, ghee, honey, sugar and the rest in order.
Having worshipped with substances consecrated by Ishana and the other mantras, in reverse for them; with all waters and incense in between, one should bathe Shiva with the root-mantra.
Having dried with barley powder, with cool waters as desired, having bathed with scented water by one's own power, with a clean cloth,
having wiped him one should give arghya; one should not move the hand over him. One should not leave the linga's head empty; one should make it with flowers and then give;
having smeared with sandal and the rest, having worshipped with flowers with the Shiva-mantra; having sprinkled the incense vessel with the missile-mantra and worshipped with the Shiva-mantra,
having taken the bell worshipped with the missile-mantra, one should give guggulu; afterward one should give rinsing water, ending with svadha, by the heart-mantra.
Having performed the lamp-waving and made him rinse again, having bowed and taken the god's permission, one should worship the enjoyment-limbs:
the heart in fire, moon-radiant, and Shiva in Ishana, golden-radiant; the crest red in the southwest, black armor in the northwest;
four-faced and four-armed, one should worship these on the petals; the missile, though terrible with fangs, in the east and others, like a thunderbolt.
